newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Foreigners seen confident in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners seen confident in Venezuela.

text.p: Record rises in Venezuelan Brady bond prices are just one of the signs of rising foreign confidence in Venezuela, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar, said: the challenge now is to transmit that to Venezuelans.
"In New York in the conversations we had with bankers and investors there was this great feeling of confidence," he told reporters after the economic cabinet's weekly meeting.
Sentiment is moving lockstep with the sustained improvement in macro-economic indicators, he added.

Central Bank operating reserves are at $8.1 billion, compared to gross reserves of $12.2 billion. "As for inflation...it continues to fall and we're sure that next month's rate of decrease will be larger than last month's," he said.
August inflation fell to 4.1 percent from 5.0 percent in July.
"However more important than these quantitative indicators... is the qualitative change in confidence towards this country," Matos added.
"Many influential people now say that Venezuela has become one of the most important places for long term investments."
